date.label: Undated Joshua narrative
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: Joshua 6 describes seven days of ritual encirclement (Joshua 6:1–16)
Jericho’s possessions are placed under herem with specified metal exceptions (Joshua 6:17–21)
Rahab and household are spared in account (Joshua 6:22–25)
Bruins and van der Plicht report a final Middle Bronze Age destruction of Tell es-Sultan during the late seventeenth or sixteenth century BCE; this does not establish Joshua 6. (Joshua 6)
claims.evidence: Bruins and van der Plicht 1995, Radiocarbon 37(2): 213–220; Kennedy 2023, Religions 14(6), article 796 (full article).

claims.claim: 1 Kings 16:34 presents Hiel’s rebuilding in relation to Joshua’s curse (Joshua 6:26; 1 Kings 16:34)

connections.note: The oath episode in Joshua 2 continues explicitly into the rescue of Rahab in Joshua 6.
The law concerning separation and destruction in Deuteronomy 7 provides the literary and legal context for Joshua 6.
1 Kings 16:34 retrospectively links Hiel's rebuilding of Jericho to the curse in Joshua 6:26, as narrative fulfilment rather than a prediction issued by 1 Kings.
Hebrews 11:30 interprets the fall of Jericho in a later theological catalogue of faith.
